title: A student diet
paragraphs: Starting at university or college can be a big challenge, especially if you’re living away from home for the first time. You're faced with big questions such as, ‘Who's going to do my washing?’ ‘Who's going to tidy my room?’ And, most importantly, ‘How am I going to eat?’ Yes, living on your own means you have to cook for yourself, and when you're living a student lifestyle, this could be a recipe for disaster.

Students, in the UK at least, often rely on staples such as baked beans or cheese on toast. And for the more adventurous, there's 'spag bol’ – spaghetti bolognaise - a budget-friendly bowl of minced beef cooked in a tomato sauce, served on a bed of spaghetti. If you make a huge pan of it, you can probably make it last a whole week! Other low-cost options include jar sauces and oven pizzas.

Recently, a British supermarket suggested that rose harissa paste, organic cider vinegar and Swiss bouillon powder were the essential ingredients needed for the 'student store cupboard'. But are these items considered essential and affordable for someone on a budget?

Catrin Stewart is 20 and in her final year at the University of Manchester and is currently food editor of the student paper. She told BBC News that "I'm in a unique position… I'm in a house of eight people and six are vegan. We have to be quite inventive with our food. We have lots of Asian influences, lots of experimenting." Another student, Eleanor, is vegetarian and finds this meat-free food "easier and less expensive".

Living on a limited budget is certainly one obstacle to eating a well-balanced diet – some young people also have limited culinary expertise and besides, there are more fun things to go and do than stay at home and cook, that's why many students survive on takeaways and microwave meals. But what should a health-conscious student really have in his or her food cupboard? Jack Monroe, a food writer and campaigner, has some advice: baked beans, stuffing, lemon juice, tinned tomatoes and tomato ketchup, described as "salt, sugar, vinegar and tomato all in one handy squeezy bottle." And if that doesn't appeal, you can always wait until you visit mum and dad for a slap-up meal!

vocabulary.term: recipe for disaster [ˈresəpi fɔː(r) dɪˈzɑːstə(r)] 灾难的根源；祸根
vocabulary.entry: recipe for disaster [ˈresəpi fɔː(r) dɪˈzɑːstə(r)] 灾难的根源；祸根
vocabulary.example: Going to the supermarket when I'm really hungry, and without a shopping list, is a recipe for disaster.
vocabulary.translation: 饿着肚子又没带购物清单去超市，注定会酿成麻烦。

vocabulary.term: staple [ˈsteɪpl] n. 主食；主要产品
vocabulary.entry: staple [ˈsteɪpl] n. 主食；主要产品
vocabulary.example: For nearly a billion people around the world, cassava is a staple crop and a primary source of calories.
vocabulary.translation: 全球约有10亿人将木薯当作主食作物，它也是这些人热量的主要来源。

vocabulary.term: budget-friendly [ˈbʌdʒɪt ˈfrendli] adj. 经济实惠的；便宜的
vocabulary.entry: budget-friendly [ˈbʌdʒɪt ˈfrendli] adj. 经济实惠的；便宜的
vocabulary.example: Try some of its restaurants: the food is delicious and very budget-friendly.
vocabulary.translation: 去试试那里的几家餐馆吧，那里的食物美味又经济实惠。

vocabulary.term: minced beef [mɪnst biːf] 碎牛肉；牛肉末
vocabulary.entry: minced beef [mɪnst biːf] 碎牛肉；牛肉末
vocabulary.example: Add the lean minced beef and fry for 5 mins.
vocabulary.translation: 加入瘦牛肉末，煎5分钟。

vocabulary.term: harissa paste [həˈriːsə peɪst] 哈里萨酱（北非辣味酱料）
vocabulary.entry: harissa paste [həˈriːsə peɪst] 哈里萨酱（北非辣味酱料）
vocabulary.example: Mix the harissa paste with the vinegar.
vocabulary.translation: 把哈里萨酱和醋混合在一起。

vocabulary.term: cider vinegar [ˈsaɪdə(r) ˈvɪnɪɡə(r)] 苹果醋
vocabulary.entry: cider vinegar [ˈsaɪdə(r) ˈvɪnɪɡə(r)] 苹果醋
vocabulary.example: Cider vinegar is used to preserve and pickle vegetables, or added to sauces and salads.
vocabulary.translation: 苹果醋可用于腌制蔬菜，也可添加到调味汁和沙拉中。

vocabulary.term: bouillon powder [ˈbuːjɒn ˈpaʊdə(r)] 肉汤粉；高汤粉
vocabulary.entry: bouillon powder [ˈbuːjɒn ˈpaʊdə(r)] 肉汤粉；高汤粉
vocabulary.example: Chicken bouillon powder is a convenient seasoning for making quick and flavorful soups.
vocabulary.translation: 鸡精粉是一种便捷的调味品，可用于快速做出味道鲜美的汤。

vocabulary.term: vegan [ˈviːɡən] n. 纯素食主义者
vocabulary.entry: vegan [ˈviːɡən] n. 纯素食主义者
vocabulary.example: As a vegan, she doesn't eat any meat, eggs or dairy products.
vocabulary.translation: 作为纯素食主义者，她不吃任何肉类、蛋类和奶制品。

vocabulary.term: inventive [ɪnˈventɪv] adj. 有创意的；善于创新的
vocabulary.entry: inventive [ɪnˈventɪv] adj. 有创意的；善于创新的
vocabulary.example: The company was known for hiring inventive people who could dream up new products.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司以招聘那些能构思出新产品的创新型人才而闻名。

vocabulary.term: vegetarian [ˌvedʒəˈteəriən] n. 素食主义者
vocabulary.entry: vegetarian [ˌvedʒəˈteəriən] n. 素食主义者
vocabulary.example: My sister has been a vegetarian for years and gets all her protein from beans and nuts.
vocabulary.translation: 我姐姐吃素好几年了，她所需的蛋白质都来自豆类和坚果。

vocabulary.term: well-balanced diet [ˌwel ˈbælənst ˈdaɪət] 均衡饮食
vocabulary.entry: well-balanced diet [ˌwel ˈbælənst ˈdaɪət] 均衡饮食
vocabulary.example: A well-balanced diet can increase resistance to disease and improve management of chronic health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡的饮食能增强抗病能力，并有助于慢性疾病的调理。

vocabulary.term: culinary expertise [ˈkʌlɪnəri ˈekspɜːtɪz] 烹饪技能；厨艺
vocabulary.entry: culinary expertise [ˈkʌlɪnəri ˈekspɜːtɪz] 烹饪技能；厨艺
vocabulary.example: I would openly praise her culinary expertise, without fear of earning my wife's scorn.
vocabulary.translation: 我会毫不避讳地称赞她的厨艺，丝毫不怕惹我妻子不高兴。

vocabulary.term: takeaway [ˈteɪkəweɪ] n. 外卖食品；外卖餐馆
vocabulary.entry: takeaway [ˈteɪkəweɪ] n. 外卖食品；外卖餐馆
vocabulary.example: I ordered a takeaway pizza because I didn't feel like cooking tonight.
vocabulary.translation: 我点了一份外卖披萨，因为我今晚不想做饭。

vocabulary.term: health-conscious [ˈhelθ ˈkɒnʃəs] adj. 注重健康的
vocabulary.entry: health-conscious [ˈhelθ ˈkɒnʃəs] adj. 注重健康的
vocabulary.example: Health-conscious consumers are increasingly choosing organic produce over chemically treated food.
vocabulary.translation: 注重健康的消费者正越来越多地选择有机农产品，而非经化学处理的食品。

vocabulary.term: tinned tomatoes [tɪnd təˈmɑːtəʊz] n. 罐装番茄（复数）
vocabulary.entry: tinned tomatoes [tɪnd təˈmɑːtəʊz] n. 罐装番茄（复数）
vocabulary.example: Add tinned tomatoes, chilli powder and ground cumin, then season with pepper.
vocabulary.translation: 加入罐装番茄、辣椒粉和孜然粉，再撒点胡椒粉调味。

vocabulary.term: tomato ketchup [təˈmɑːtəʊ ˈketʃəp] 番茄酱
vocabulary.entry: tomato ketchup [təˈmɑːtəʊ ˈketʃəp] 番茄酱
vocabulary.example: He squirted some tomato ketchup on his fries before taking a bite.
vocabulary.translation: 他在薯条上挤了些番茄酱，然后才咬了一口。

vocabulary.term: slap-up meal [ˈslæp ʌp miːl] 美餐；盛宴（非正式）
vocabulary.entry: slap-up meal [ˈslæp ʌp miːl] 美餐；盛宴（非正式）
vocabulary.example: We had a slap-up meal at a fancy restaurant to celebrate our anniversary.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在一家高档餐厅吃了一顿丰盛的大餐，以此庆祝我们的纪念日。

vocabulary.term: survive on [səˈvaɪv ɒn] 靠……维持生活；靠……生存
vocabulary.entry: survive on [səˈvaɪv ɒn] 靠……维持生活；靠……生存
vocabulary.example: Many animals survive on very little water in the desert.
vocabulary.translation: 许多动物在沙漠中仅靠少量水分就能生存。

vocabulary.term: experimenting [ɪkˈsperɪmentɪŋ] v. 尝试；实验（experiment的现在分词）
vocabulary.entry: experimenting [ɪkˈsperɪmentɪŋ] v. 尝试；实验（experiment的现在分词）
vocabulary.example: In 1857 Mendel started experimenting with peas in his monastery garden.
vocabulary.translation: 1857年，孟德尔开始在修道院的菜园里用豌豆做实验。

vocabulary.term: limited budget [ˈlɪmɪtɪd ˈbʌdʒɪt] 有限预算
vocabulary.entry: limited budget [ˈlɪmɪtɪd ˈbʌdʒɪt] 有限预算
vocabulary.example: We have to cut some costs because we're working with a limited budget this year.
vocabulary.translation: 今年我们的预算有限，所以必须削减部分开支。

sentences.chinese: 我和八个人同住，其中六人是纯素食主义者。
